answer: Because the glacier calculation reruns each epoch, the sparrow weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the sable settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 129 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 53% independent neighbours on the funding graph. That is 23 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
